It feels pointless, like it doesn’t matter if I show up because everything is heading toward some kind of collapse anyway. I’m convinced something terrible is coming, like the world is winding down, and I can’t shake that idea.

For about eight months I’ve also had these strange sensations, like something crawling under my skin or brushing my arms when no one is there. When I try to talk about all of this, my words get jumbled—my husband says I start stringing odd phrases together that don’t make sense. Around the same time, I started getting it into my head that my late husband had someone else before he died, that he’d been sneaking around then. I keep going over old receipts, photos, convinced there were affairs, even though I know that makes no sense now. Sometimes I feel like something is crawling on my arms or brushing my face when nothing’s there.

Lately, for about six months, it’s swung the other way. Most days feel hollow, like I’m just going through the motions. I don’t enjoy knitting, church, or seeing the grandchildren.
